newsitem.title: USA: Listless U.S. Treasuries cue emerging debt losses.
newsitem.headline: Listless U.S. Treasuries cue emerging debt losses.

text.p: Most emerging market debt traded lower Tuesday, following the lead of U.S. Treasuries, market experts said.
"Right now the market looks tired, and the (U.S. Treasury) bond is not helping much," one Brady trader said. "It's not surprising after last week's gains."
Spreads over Treasuries generally widened except for those of a few issues that handily outperformed the U.S. market.
Among Brady bonds, Brazil "C" bonds BR8D14=RR were off 1/2 at 79-7/8 bid and Argentina FRBs ARFLC05=RR were off 1/8 at 93-7/8 bid. Argentina's global 2017 was off 3/8 at 109-3/4.
Venezuela traded lower despite pricing its new global bond at the high end of market expectations.
The $315 million 10-year bond priced at 265 basis points over comparable Treasuries. Analysts had expected a starting spread of 265 to 270 basis points over.
Rumors that the country might use proceeds of the global bond to buy back Bradies appeared unfounded, traders said.
"I think it is a little too much rumor. You need to have something behind it to justify the continuation of the rally," one trader said.
In late trading, Venezuela FLIRBs VZ6C97=RR were off 7/8 at 92-1/4 bid, and pars VZ675C20=RR were off 7/8 at 77-7/8.
Ecuador racked up the day's largest gains, tightening more than 50 basis points in some issues largely because of technical factors, traders and analysts said.
Ecuador PDIs ECPDI=RR were up 3/4 at 67-1/8 bid, while discounts ECDISC=RR climbed 1-5/8 to 73-3/8 bid.
"A good part of it is technical trading. PDIs broke their historic high and then it just catapulted," said Siobhan Manning, senior Latin America analyst at Santander Investments.
PDIs breached their closing-basis high of 66-1/2 set on January 23, she said.
An Ecuadorean newspaper said President Fabian Alarcon planned to unveil a deficit-trimming plan by Thursday, but such fundamental news had little impact, experts said.
"Ultimately, the fundamentals are relatively unchanged," Manning said. "Any positive outcome from the fiscal measures is already priced in."
Elsewhere, Mexico pars MX625L19=RR were off 1/2 at 76-3/8 bid, Bulgaria IABs BGLFTH11=RR were up 3/8 at 69 and dollar-denominated Russian Vnesh loans were unchanged at 89-1/2 bid.
